item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 101150
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM PDT Sat Oct 10 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Rachel, located several hundred miles southwest of Punta
Baja, Mexico, and on Hurricane Simon, located about one hundred
miles south-southwest of Manzanillo, Mexico.

South of Southwestern Mexico:
An area of low pressure is forecast to develop south or southwest of
the coast of Mexico by early next week. Environmental conditions are
expected to be conducive for gradual development thereafter, and a
tropical depression is likely to form by the middle or latter half
of next week as the system moves generally west-northwestward at
around 10 mph.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...70 percent.

$$
Forecaster Papin

item.title: Tropical Storm Rachel Public Advisory Number 54
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM PDT Sat Oct 10 2026 
000
WTPZ33 KNHC 101452
TCPEP3
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Rachel Advisory Number  54
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
800 AM PDT Sat Oct 10 2026
 
...TROPICAL STORM CONDITIONS EXPECTED TO BEGIN ON THE WEST COAST OF
THE BAJA CALIFORNIA PENINSULA BY THIS EVENING...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 AM PDT...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...25.5N 119.6W
ABOUT 390 MI...625 KM SW OF PUNTA BAJA MEXICO
ABOUT 520 MI...835 KM SSW OF SAN DIEGO CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...60 MPH...95 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NE OR 55 DEGREES AT 22 MPH...35 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...992 MB...29.30 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
The government of Mexico has extended the Tropical Storm Warning
along the west coast of the Baja California peninsula southward to 
Punta Eugenia.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for...
* West coast of Baja California and Baja California Sur, from Punta
Eugenia northward to the U.S./Mexico Border
* East coast of Baja California, from Isla San Luis northward to
Puerto Penasco
 
A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for...
* Southern California coast from the U.S/Mexico Border northward to
the San Diego/Orange County Line
* East coast of Baja California, from Bahia De Los Angeles
northward to Isla San Luis
* Northwest Mexico from Puerto Libertad to Puerto Penasco
 
A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected somewhere within the warning area, in this case within 12
to 24 hours.
 
A Tropical Storm Watch means that tropical storm conditions are
possible within the watch area, in this case within 24 hours.
 
For storm information specific to your area in the United
States, including possible inland watches and warnings, please
monitor products issued by your local National Weather Service
forecast office. For storm information specific to your area
outside of the United States, please monitor products issued by
your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 AM PDT (1500 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Rachel was
located near latitude 25.5 North, longitude 119.6 West. Rachel is
moving toward the northeast near 22 mph (35 km/h). A northeastward 
to north-northeastward motion with an increase in forward speed is 
expected through Sunday. On the forecast track, the center of Rachel 
is expected to approach northern Baja California today and move 
onshore tonight. Rachel's post-tropical remnants will then move 
across the southwestern United States on Sunday.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 60 mph (95 km/h) with higher gusts.
Some strengthening is possible through tonight, but rapid weakening 
is expected after Rachel moves inland over Baja California and the 
southwestern United States on Sunday. Rachel is likely to become 
post-tropical by Sunday morning.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 150 miles (240 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 992 mb (29.30 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Rachel can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP3 and WMO header WTPZ43 KNHC.
 
WIND: Tropical storm conditions are expected to reach portions of
the Baja California Peninsula within the Tropical Storm Warning area
beginning this evening and continuing into Sunday morning. Tropical
storm conditions are also possible within the Tropical Storm Watch
area in extreme Southern California, eastern Baja California, and
portions of northwest Mexico beginning tonight or early Sunday.
Strong gusty winds associated with the system are expected to spread
over interior portions of the Southwest United States, especially in
areas of higher terrain, tonight through early next week.
 
RAINFALL: Rachel will bring 1 to 3 inches of rain to portions of 
Baja California this weekend.

Rachel and its associated moisture will also bring rainfall of 1 to 
3 inches, with maximum amounts locally up to 5 inches in portions of 
the Southwest United States this weekend. This will lead to 
increasing coverage of rainfall and potential for significant flash 
and urban flooding.

For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with 
Rachel, please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall 
Graphic available at
hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep3.shtml?rainqpf and the Flash Flood Risk 
graphic at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep3.shtml?ero.
 
SURF: Waves generated by Rachel will continue to build along the
coasts of Southern California and northern Baja California today.
These waves, combined with an incoming long-period southerly swell,
will cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Coastal
flooding and erosion are expected to worsen tonight into Sunday
morning as the highest waves coincide with the high tides and water
levels that are already running well above predicted levels.
Moderate to major coastal flooding is expected, with hazardous
coastal conditions continuing into early next week. Please consult
products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next intermediate advisory at 1100 AM PDT.
Next complete advisory at 200 PM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Berg
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Tropical Storm Rachel Forecast Discussion Number 54
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM PDT Sat Oct 10 2026 
000
WTPZ43 KNHC 101453
TCDEP3
 
Tropical Storm Rachel Discussion Number  54
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
800 AM PDT Sat Oct 10 2026
 
Rachel appears to be in the midst of its transition to a 
post-tropical storm. Convection is becoming shallower and is being 
sheared off to the northeast of the center due to 25-35 kt of 
southwesterly shear, and the system is taking on a 
frontal structure with a drier air mass of stratocumulus 
clouds wrapping around the southern side of the circulation. Based 
on the ASCAT-B scatterometer pass from overnight, the initial 
intensity is held at 50 kt.

Rachel has been moving a bit east of the previous track, and the 
current motion is estimated to be northeastward, or 055/19 kt. A 
turn toward the north-northeast with an increase in forward speed 
is expected by tonight while Rachel interacts with a mid-level 
cut-off low located to its northwest. The track guidance is in good 
agreement that Rachel's center will move onshore the extreme 
northern portion of Baja California tonight, with the system 
continuing quickly north-northeastward across the southwestern U.S. 
on Sunday. The new NHC track forecast has been nudged east of the 
previous track and is close to the latest HCCA aid.
 
Model-derived phase space diagrams indicate that Rachel now has an 
asymmetric, shallow warm-core structure and is likely to become 
deeper cold core, and hence fully post tropical, in about 24 hours 
once it has moved onshore. In the meantime, baroclinic interaction 
with the upper-level trough could cause some slight intensification 
over the next 12 hours or so, which is supported by much of the 
intensity models. Weakening is expected after Rachel moves onshore, 
although strong gusty winds are likely across much of the 
southwestern U.S. through early next week as low pressure moves 
into the Rocky Mountains. A 36-hour post-tropical point is provided 
for continuity, but it's likely that the low will not have a 
well-defined circulation by that point.
 
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Rachel is expected to approach and move ashore along the coast of
northern Baja California at tropical storm strength tonight. 
Tropical storm conditions are expected in portions of Baja 
California and northern Baja California Sur, Mexico, where Tropical 
Storm Warnings are in effect. Tropical storm conditions are also 
possible in extreme Southern California, eastern Baja California, 
and portions of northwestern Mexico where Tropical Storm Watches are 
in effect.
 
2. Damaging wind gusts associated with Rachel and its remnants are
expected to spread over portions of northwestern Mexico and interior
portions of the Southwest United States, especially in areas of
higher terrain, tonight and Sunday.
 
3. Rachel and its moisture will continue to spread over portions of 
the Southwest United States and northern Baja California peninsula. 
This will lead to increasing coverage of rainfall and for the 
potential for significant flash and urban flooding this weekend.
 
4. Waves generated by Rachel, combined with an incoming long-period
southerly swell, will produce life-threatening surf and rip current
conditions along the coasts of Southern California and northern Baja
California. Major coastal flooding has already been occurring in
some areas, with observed water levels running as much as 1.5 feet
above predictions. Coastal flooding and erosion are expected to
worsen tonight into Sunday morning as the highest waves associated
with Rachel coincide with high tides and already elevated water
levels. Hazardous coastal conditions are expected to continue into
early next week. Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  10/1500Z 25.5N 119.6W   50 KT  60 MPH
 12H  11/0000Z 28.2N 117.5W   55 KT  65 MPH
 24H  11/1200Z 33.0N 115.3W   40 KT  45 MPH...POST-TROP/INLAND
 36H  12/0000Z 38.5N 112.5W   30 KT  35 MPH...POST-TROP/INLAND
 48H  12/1200Z...DISSIPATED
 
$$
Forecaster Berg

item.description:

BULLETIN
Hurricane Simon Advisory Number  13
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
900 AM CST Sat Oct 10 2026
 
...SIMON A DANGEROUS CATEGORY 4 HURRICANE WITH 150-MPH WINDS...
...PREPARATIONS TO PROTECT LIFE AND PROPERTY SHOULD BE RUSHED TO
COMPLETION SHORTLY IN THE HURRICANE WARNING AREA...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 900 AM CST...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...17.4N 104.8W
ABOUT 115 MI...185 KM SSW OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
ABOUT 215 MI...345 KM SSE OF CABO CORRIENTES MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...150 MPH...240 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...N OR 350 DEGREES AT 3 MPH...6 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...938 MB...27.70 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
None.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Hurricane Warning is in effect for...
* Punta San Telmo to El Roblito
* Las Islas Marias
 
A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for...
* East of Punta San Telmo to Lazaro Cardenas
 
A Hurricane Warning means that hurricane conditions are expected
somewhere within the warning area. A warning is typically issued 36
hours before the anticipated first occurrence of
tropical-storm-force winds, conditions that make outside
preparations difficult or dangerous. Preparations to protect life
and property should be rushed to completion today.
 
A Tropical Storm Watch means that tropical storm conditions are
possible within the watch area, in this case starting this
afternoon.
 
Additional watches or warnings could be required for portions of the
coast of southwestern and west-central Mexico later today.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 900 AM CST (1500 UTC), the center of Hurricane Simon was located 
near latitude 17.4 North, longitude 104.8 West. Simon is moving 
toward the north near 5 mph (7 km/h), and this general motion is 
forecast to continue through the weekend. On the forecast track, 
Simon is expected to be near or just inland of the west-central 
coast of Mexico on Sunday.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 150 mph (240 km/h) with higher
gusts. Simon is a category 4 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson
Hurricane Wind Scale. Some additional strengthening remains
possible today, and Simon is forecast to approach the coast of
west-central Mexico as a major hurricane tonight or early
Sunday. An Air Force Reconnaissance aircraft is scheduled to
investigate the hurricane later today.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 15 miles (30 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 125 miles
(205 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 938 mb (27.70 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Simon can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP5 and WMO header WTPZ45 KNHC.
 
WIND: Hurricane conditions are expected in the southern part of the
Hurricane Warning area beginning early Sunday, with tropical storm
conditions expected as soon as this afternoon, with these winds
spreading northward thereafter. Tropical storm conditions are
possible within the Tropical Storm Watch area beginning this
afternoon.
 
RAINFALL: Simon is expected to produce rainfall totals of 10 to 20
inches over portions of southwestern Mexico, with isolated maximum
totals of 30 inches possible across portions of Michoacan, Colima,
and Jalisco through Sunday. This rainfall will produce
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of
steep terrain.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Simon,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep5.shtml?rainqpf.
 
STORM SURGE: A dangerous storm surge is expected along the
immediate coast near and to the east of where the center makes
landfall. Near the coast, the surge will be accompanied by large and
destructive waves.
 
SURF:  Swells generated by Simon will affect portions of the coast
of southwestern and west-central Mexico during the next few days.
These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions. Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next intermediate advisory at 1200 PM CST.
Next complete advisory at 300 PM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Papin

item.title: Hurricane Simon Forecast Discussion Number 12
item.description:
Issued at 300 AM CST Sat Oct 10 2026 
000
WTPZ45 KNHC 100857
TCDEP5
 
Hurricane Simon Discussion Number  12
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP202026
300 AM CST Sat Oct 10 2026
 
The very small inner-core of Simon remains very impressive as the
cyclone has continued to strengthen. The proxy-visible imagery has
started to show that the tiny eye of the hurricane is clearing
out.  The most recent TAFB Dvorak fix was a T6.0/115 kt,
while the objective raw T-number intensity estimates  from
UW-CIMSS have ranged from 120 to 132 kt. Based on a blend of the
objective and subjective intensity estimates, the initial intensity
has been increased to 125 kt for this advisory.  The wind radii has
been adjusted based on a recent ASCAT pass.
 
The hurricane is expected to continue to rapidly strengthen over
the next day or so, with a peak intensity of 135 kt forecast. Given
the small size of the inner core, there is a higher than normal
degree of uncertainty with the peak intensity. Therefore, it is
possible that Simon could become stronger than what is forecast.
Only a few changes were made for the current NHC forecast compared
to the previous forecast.
 
Simon's initial motion is estimated at 360/4 kt, northward.
The hurricane is being steered by the southerly mid-level flow
produced by high pressure over southern Mexico and a longwave
mid-tropospheric trough to the west stretching south-southwestward
from the southwest United States. There is still some uncertainty
about the track for Simon, as most of the skilled model guidance
including HCCA and GDMI forecast aids have been experiencing to the
left of the track bias. The current NHC track forecast has the
hurricane move inland over the Mexican states of Colima and
Jalisco; however, it is possible that the cyclone could remain just
offshore as it moves generally northward. Should Simon move inland,
then it should dissipate quickly due to the mountainous terrain.
However, if Simon were to stay offshore, then it would maintain
hurricane intensity for a longer period of time. The current track
forecast is similar to the previous one, with only a few small
adjustments being made.
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Catastrophic wind and life-threatening storm surge impacts are
likely along a portion of the west-central coast of Mexico, and a
Hurricane warning is in effect from Punta San Telmo to Punta Mita.
Preparations to protect life and property should be completed
today.
 
2. Heavy rainfall associated with Simon will impact portions of
southwestern Mexico through this weekend. This rainfall will produce
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of
steep terrain.
 
3. Swells will affect portions of the southwestern and west-central
coast of Mexico through the weekend. These swells are likely to
cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please
consult products from your local weather office.
